summary.native: near the beginning of a time; before the usual or expected time; from the first stage

etymology.ko: 고대 영어 부사 ǣrlīce에서 왔다. ǣr(일찍, 전에)에 부사를 만드는 -līce(오늘날의 -ly)가 붙은 말이고, 형용사 ǣrlic도 고대 영어에 있었다. ǣr는 게르만 조어 *airiz에서 왔으며, 더 거슬러 올라가면 '낮, 아침'을 뜻하는 인도유럽어 뿌리와 이어진다고 본다. 옛말 ere(~하기 전에)와 erstwhile(이전의)이 같은 식구다. '일찍 일어나는 새가 벌레를 잡는다(The early bird catches the worm)'라는 속담은 1670년대부터 기록되어 있다.
etymology.native: From the Old English adverb ærlice, made of ær 'soon, before' + -lice (modern -ly). The adjective ærlic also existed in Old English. Ær comes from Proto-Germanic *airiz and is traced to an older root meaning 'day, morning'. The old word ere 'before' and erstwhile 'former' are relatives. The saying The early bird catches the worm is recorded from the 1670s.

grammar.ko: 형용사와 부사의 꼴이 같다. -ly로 끝나지만 형용사로도 쓴다: an early train(형용사) / leave early(부사).
grammar.native: The adjective and adverb have the same form. It ends in -ly but is also an adjective: an early train (adjective), leave early (adverb).

grammar.ko: 비교급·최상급은 earlier, earliest(y를 i로 바꾼다). at the earliest는 '빨라도, 아무리 일러도'.
grammar.native: Comparative and superlative: earlier, earliest (y changes to i). At the earliest means 'not before this time'.

grammar.ko: 부사 earlier는 '아까, 앞서, 전에'라는 뜻으로 아주 흔하다: as I said earlier(앞서 말했듯이), earlier today(오늘 아까).
grammar.native: The adverb earlier very often means 'at a time before now': as I said earlier, earlier today.

grammar.ko: 시기의 앞부분은 두 가지로 말한다: early in + 기간(early in May) / in early + 기간(in early May). 둘 다 '5월 초에'.
grammar.native: There are two patterns for the start of a period: early in + time (early in May) and in early + time (in early May). Both mean the same.

meaning.native: near the beginning of a period of time, an event, or someone's life

usage.ko: 하루·해·시대·나이·일의 앞부분을 가리킨다. the early morning(이른 아침), the early 2000s(2000년대 초), in your early twenties(20대 초반)처럼 명사 앞에 쓴다.
usage.native: Used for the first part of a day, year, period, age, or piece of work. It comes before a noun: the early morning, the early 2000s, in your early twenties.

examples.text: I love the quiet of the early morning.
My parents moved to Seoul in the early 1990s.
He started his own company in his early thirties.
The project is still at an early stage.

meaning.native: arriving, happening, or done before the usual or expected time

usage.ko: 정해진 시각이나 보통 때보다 먼저일 때 쓴다. be동사 뒤에 오거나(You're early.) 명사 앞에 온다(an early lunch, early retirement). 격식 있는 글에서는 '되도록 빠른'의 뜻으로도 쓴다(at your earliest convenience).
usage.native: Used when something comes or happens before the planned or usual time. It can follow be (You're early.) or come before a noun (an early lunch, early retirement). In formal writing it can mean 'as soon as possible': at your earliest convenience.

examples.text: You're early! The meeting doesn't start until ten.
Let's have an early lunch before the crowds come.
examples.ko: 사람들이 몰리기 전에 점심을 좀 일찍 먹읍시다.

examples.text: I'm tired, so I'm going to have an early night.
Please reply at your earliest convenience.
examples.ko: 편하실 때 되도록 빨리 회신 부탁드립니다.

meaning.native: belonging to the first stage in the development of something

usage.ko: 기술·예술·역사가 막 시작된 무렵의 것을 가리킨다. early computers(초창기 컴퓨터), her early works(그녀의 초기 작품)처럼 명사 앞에 쓴다.
usage.native: Used for things from the first stage of a technology, an art, or history. It comes before a noun: early computers, her early works.

examples.text: Early computers were as big as a room.
I like the band's early songs better.
examples.ko: 나는 그 밴드의 초기 노래가 더 좋다.

examples.text: Early humans used simple stone tools.
examples.ko: 초기 인류는 간단한 돌 도구를 썼다.

meaning.native: near the beginning of a period of time or an event

usage.ko: early in + 기간(early in the morning, early next week) 꼴이 흔하다. early on은 '초반에, 일찍부터'라는 뜻이다.
usage.native: Often used in the pattern early in + time (early in the morning) or before next and last (early next week). Early on means 'near the start'.

examples.text: The accident happened early in the morning.
We'll send you the details early next week.
examples.ko: 자세한 내용은 다음 주 초에 보내 드리겠습니다.

examples.text: I realized early on that this job wasn't for me.
examples.ko: 이 일이 나와 맞지 않는다는 걸 초반에 알았다.

meaning.native: before the usual or expected time

usage.ko: 동사 뒤에 와서 보통보다 이른 때에 하는 것을 말한다. get up early, leave early, arrive early가 흔하다. 얼마나 이른지는 앞에 붙인다(ten minutes early).
usage.native: Used after a verb to show that something is done before the usual time: get up early, leave early, arrive early. Put the amount of time first: ten minutes early.

examples.text: I have to get up early tomorrow to catch my flight.
examples.ko: 내일 비행기를 타야 해서 일찍 일어나야 해.

examples.text: Can I leave work early today? I have a doctor's appointment.
examples.ko: 오늘 일찍 퇴근해도 될까요? 병원 예약이 있어서요.

examples.text: Book early to get the best seats.
The train arrived ten minutes early.

cautions.ko: 한국어 '빨리'는 '일찍'과 '빠르게'를 다 뜻하지만 영어는 나눈다. early는 시간상 일찍, quickly·fast는 속도가 빠르게, soon은 머지않아. Come early.(일찍 와) / Come quickly.(서둘러 와) / Come back soon.(곧 돌아와)
cautions.native: Early is about time, quickly and fast are about speed, and soon means 'in a short time from now'. Come early. Come quickly. Come back soon.

cautions.ko: '아까 전화했었어'는 I called you earlier.다. I called you early.라고 하면 '이른 시간에 전화했다'가 된다.
cautions.native: To mean 'some time before now', use earlier: I called you earlier. I called you early means you called at an early hour.

cautions.ko: 나이·연대의 '초반·중반·후반'은 early·mid·late로 말한다: in her early thirties(30대 초반), in the late 1990s(1990년대 후반).
cautions.native: For parts of an age or period, use early, mid, and late: in her early thirties, in the mid-1990s, in the late 1990s.

cautions.ko: 시계가 '빠르다'는 early가 아니라 fast다: My watch is five minutes fast.(내 시계는 5분 빠르다)
cautions.native: For a clock that shows a later time than the real one, use fast, not early: My watch is five minutes fast.

note.ko: 어떤 기간의 앞부분을 가리키는 틀이다. morning, week, career처럼 기간을 뜻하는 말이 온다.
note.native: Points to the first part of a period, with words such as morning, week, or career.

patterns.example: Early in the week we still had plenty of time.

note.ko: 나이를 대략 말하는 틀이다. twenties, thirties처럼 열 단위 복수형이 온다.
note.native: Gives an approximate age. A plural ten-year word follows, such as twenties or thirties.

patterns.example: He bought the house in his early forties.
patterns.example_ko: 그는 사십 대 초반에 그 집을 샀다.

note.ko: 예정보다 얼마나 이른지를 숫자로 앞에 밝힌다. late도 같은 꼴로 쓴다.
note.native: A number before early says how much sooner than planned something is. Late works in the same way.

patterns.example: The train pulled in ten minutes early.

note.ko: 보통보다 이르게 하는 일을 명사로 묶는 틀이다. lunch, night, retirement처럼 때와 얽힌 말이 온다.
note.native: Packs the idea of doing something sooner than usual into a noun phrase, with words such as lunch, night, or retirement.

patterns.example: Let's have an early lunch and beat the crowd.
patterns.example_ko: 일찍 점심 먹고 붐비기 전에 나가자.

difference.ko: soon은 지금부터 얼마 지나지 않아라는 뜻이고, early는 정해진 때보다 앞선다는 뜻이다. 곧 도착한다면 soon을 쓴다.
difference.native: Soon means a short time from now, while early means before the set time. For arriving in a short while, use soon.

confusables.example: I'll be there soon, probably a little early.

difference.ko: former는 예전의, 전임의라는 뜻으로 지금은 아니라는 말이다. 시기의 앞부분을 뜻하는 early와 자리가 다르다.
difference.native: Former means previous or no longer in the role, which is different from early, the first part of a period.

confusables.example: In her early years she met a former president.

difference.ko: quickly는 속도가 빠르다는 뜻이고, early는 시간이 이르다는 뜻이다. 일찍 와서 천천히 먹을 수도 있다.
difference.native: Quickly is about speed and early is about time, so you can come early and still eat slowly.

confusables.example: He came early but finished his meal quickly.
